text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming.responses.p99 > 2.5s for 3m (SLO 1.0s). affected route: /v1/streams/generate (us-east-1). paging: #pager oncall. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/g/streaming/latency?panelId=9

emma (oncall-sre): I’m on it. seeing the alert, grabbing traces. any customer-facing impact yet?
luis (support): two customers reported aborted streams and client errors ~15m ago. support tickets linked: SUP-1892, SUP-1893. Both on hosted API.
dinesh (eng-runtime): looking at runtime tail traces now — p95 okay but p99 is huge, looks like a small subset of requests hitting huge buffering delays in proxy -> runtime handshake. suspect slowconsumers/backpressure.
ben (eng-proxy): I’m seeing proxy downstream write stall metrics spike, tcp_write_queue grows on some frontends. Possibly long-lived slow clients blocking worker threads.
carla (eng-platform): autoscaler shows no queue backlog for inference workers, GPU utilization normal. this points to network/proxy path.
emma (oncall-sre): ok prioritize: 1) confirm customer impact and briefly notify CS 2) mitigate to restore SLO 3) root-cause triage. I’ll open an incident page.
incident-bot: Incident created: I-2026-4601. severity: sev2. runbook: streaming-tail-latency.chrono.
luis (support): posting a quick customer status: "We’re investigating increased stream latency and aborted connections. No model output loss observed for non-streaming calls." customers want ETA.
dinesh (eng-runtime): pulled kv-cache stats — no hot-cache churn. gRPC health ok. sample trace: 
```
client->proxy (120s stalled) -> proxy tries write (EAGAIN) -> proxy holds event-loop -> backend queue ages -> backend responds with more chunks -> client finally reads after 100s -> huge tail latency
```

ben (eng-proxy): can we enable aggressive keepalive timeouts for slow clients temporarily? we have a config knob: proxy.stream_slow_consumer_timeout_ms (default 120000). propose 20000ms for 10m window.
carla (eng-platform): we can push config to edge within 2min using canary roll. recommending canary across 10% frontends first.
emma (oncall-sre): do it. @ben @carla go ahead with canary. also flip on the connection-drain metric to drop stuck streams older than 30s if they’re not reading.
ben (eng-proxy): starting canary now. command: 
```
platformctl rollout --service=proxy-edge --strategy=canary --percent=10 --set=proxy.stream_slow_consumer_timeout_ms=20000 --set=proxy.drop_stalled_streams=true
```

ben (eng-proxy): canary deployed. monitoring p99.
dinesh (eng-runtime): while that rolls, can we enable fallback routing to the lower-latency model variant for streaming (model-x-small) for affected routes? that reduces token emission latency and may avoid long-lived streams.
emma (oncall-sre): agree, fallback is low-risk and reversible. @carla please enable model fallback policy for /v1/streams/generate to variant model-x-small for 15m.
carla (eng-platform): applying policy now. policy id: pf-4721.
carla (eng-platform): policy live on 100% for that route (targeted route override).
incident-bot: Automations: canary success metrics: proxy.stream_write_blocked_count decreased by 45% on canary nodes.
ben (eng-proxy): seeing improvement on canary nodes p99 -> 0.9s. full fleet still high while rollout continues.
luis (support): relaying to customers: provisional mitigation in place, may see quick reconnects. asking for permission to post status update.
product-ops: post away, say ETA 15-30m for resolution and mention fallback model + client timeout changes.
carla (eng-platform): canary to 100% rollout started. will update when complete.
dinesh (eng-runtime): noticing some clients are using older chunking framing that interacts poorly with recent keepalive behavior. sending snippet for debug: 
```
// example: client reads with blocking read() per-chunk, not using non-blocking or streaming event loop
while (!eof) {
  read(chunk);
  // heavy processing per chunk causing backpressure
}
```
emma (oncall-sre): @dinesh good call — we should add a short-term mitigation in the docs to recommend non-blocking reads and to suggest smaller chunk sizes for heavy clients. can we also add a quickserver-side metric to count slowconsumers by client ip?
dinesh (eng-runtime): adding metric: runtime.slow_consumer_by_ip (tagged counter). pushing a lightweight probe now.
ben (eng-proxy): full rollout complete. fleet p99 now 0.95s, p95 0.35s.
incident-bot: Alert cleared: streaming.responses.p99 back under 1.0s. I-2026-4601 moving to monitoring.
luis (support): updating customer tickets: mitigation applied, please reopen if you still see aborted streams.
emma (oncall-sre): good job. we avoided broad model degradation. quick RCA pointers: root cause likely a small set of slow consumer clients combined with a proxy write stall bug that allowed slow clients to occupy event-loop longer than expected. config knobs and fallback model restored SLO.
product-ops: customers updated. any postmortem planned?
emma (oncall-sre): yes — we’ll do a 90-minute postmortem session tomorrow 10:00am ET. owners: ben (proxy), dinesh (runtime), carla (platform). action items for now:
- ben: add stricter slow-consumer default (20s) and an opt-in for very long-lived sessions.
- dinesh: emit slow_consumer_by_ip metric and collect a 24h sample.
- carla: add a safety circuit in routing to automatically fallback to lower-latency model variants if p99 streaming > 1s for 5m.
- emma: draft customer-facing timeline and postmortem blurb.

emma (oncall-sre): handing off monitoring to next shift. any objections?
product-ops: no objections. thanks team.
carla (eng-platform): logging action items to Platform board: PLAT-912.
emma (oncall-sre): closing channel for now, will re-open if regressions. :white_check_mark:
